Coarse snapshots have a proposed sharp initial-layer 2D flow prediction law with fixed-output exceptions For smooth real divergence-free unforced 2D Navier–Stokes flow on (R/2pi Z)^2 with normalized area, viscosity nu>0 and initial L2 velocity norm <=E, the supplied information is the exact square Fourier snapshot P_K u(0), with |j|_infinity<=K including the zero mode, and K,E,nu,T. The output is the entire P_K velocity path on [0,T], measured in supremum-time L2 error; unlimited predictor computation is allowed. For integer K>=16, the source gives 1e-8 E^2 min{K^2 T,1/(nu+E)} <= minimax error <=10 E^2 min{K^2 T,1/(nu+E)}. This is a source-reported full proof with informed internal cross-reconstruction, not an independently verified theorem. An observed nonzero mean is handled by a Galilean frame.

The upper predictor uses only the heat evolution of the observed snapshot. Energy, global heat-comparison and short-time estimates are combined; the unknown tail is used in the analysis, not supplied to the predictor. The lower pair has an identical zero observed snapshot and phase-opposed high-frequency vorticity packets. Many positive second-Picard interactions reach a growing O(K) output band before diffusion removes the inputs. The proof bounds the analytic nonlinear remainder at a specified short time. The corrected packet shift -33L is retained with the earlier failed -32L case, including K=31; no source history is erased.

The scope matters: this is a growing output cutoff and supremum over a shrinking initial layer. Fixed low output P_J on a zero-snapshot energy fibre has an O(K^-2) upper bound with badly E/nu-dependent constants and a matching-power four-mode lower construction. At a fixed positive terminal time the zero-snapshot full output tends to zero at O(1/K). These are different contracts, not a claim of persistent O(1) prediction failure for arbitrary low outputs or turbulence. A common bounded-noise history transcript is constructed only for the specified zero-transcript setting; it is not an all-input causal observation theorem.

A single added phase bit helps the supplied two-packet family, at precision Theta(E/K) with O(K^2) spatial samples already comparable to an FFT baseline. It does not supply acquisition of a general initial state. Sensor bandwidth, noise, delay and physical implementation remain separate from exact Fourier access; no practical simulation advantage was demonstrated. Closest source comparisons include determining modes, data assimilation and negative-Sobolev continuity. Exact priority is UNKNOWN.

Family fit: existing analysis/physics/acquisition topics. N729 concerns cumulative-strain matrix and conditional parabolic growth estimates, not this coarse-initial-state minimax problem. No dependency, correction or supersession is inferred from their shared flow terminology.

source_excerpts.text:
## Main findings

The original four-mode A5 example does give a positive-time obstruction, but its error in a **fixed** low output is of order `E²/(νK²)` at fixed `E,ν` and large `K`. A negative Sobolev estimate gives the same cutoff power for every smooth initial field with zero coarse snapshot. Thus the derivative calculation cannot establish a cutoff-independent error in that fixed output.

The actual A5 target is larger: it predicts **all of the growing projection `P_K`**, with a supremum over the whole interval starting at zero. For that target a coherent packet of `O(K²)` unresolved modes gives a cutoff-independent obstruction. A matching upper uses the heat evolution of the observed fluctuation, transported by the observed mean. The exact parameter scaling in the unforced model, including arbitrary coarse snapshots and means, is established here up to explicit universal constants:

\[
10^{-8}E^2\min\{K^2T,(\nu+E)^{-1}\}
\ \le\ \mathfrak E_K^0(T;E,\nu)
\ \le\ \mathcal E_K(T;E,\nu,f=0)
\ \le\ 10E^2\min\{K^2T,(\nu+E)^{-1}\},\qquad K\ge16.
\tag{1}
\]

The constants are deliberately conservative. The lower is a genuine PDE estimate with a controlled nonlinear remainder, not a Galerkin simulation. The viscosity is the same fixed positive number throughout. The lower occurs at a time of order `K^{-2}` and in modes with frequencies of order `K`. It **does not** imply constant error at a fixed terminal time `T>0`. In the zero-snapshot fibre, a uniform terminal-time upper bound below tends to zero.

The restriction is **zero forcing**, an explicit allowed supplied forcing. The upper handles every coarse snapshot, while the lower already occurs on the zero-snapshot fibre. No corresponding law for arbitrary nonzero forcing is claimed.

## 1. Contract and normalization

Work on `(R/2πZ)^2` with normalized area measure, so Parseval reads

\[
\|u\|_2^2=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z^2}|u_j|^2.
\]

All initial fields are real, smooth and divergence free. There is no forcing. The derivations in §§2–5 use mean-zero fields; the exact Galilean extension in §3 covers arbitrary means, which A5's original displayed class permits. Let `u(t;u0)` be the unique classical 2D solution of

\[
u_t+\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)=\nu\Delta u,
\quad \operatorname{div}u=0,\quad \nu>0.
\]

## 2. A negative Sobolev estimate for the entire zero-snapshot fibre

Let `A=-Δ` on mean-zero divergence-free fields and put

\[
X(t)=\|u(t)\|_2^2,\quad Z(t)=\|\nabla u(t)\|_2^2,
\quad Y(t)=\|A^{-1/2}u(t)\|_2^2.
\]

The ordinary energy identity gives

\[
X(t)\le E^2,\qquad \int_0^\infty Z(t)\,dt\le {E^2\over2\nu}.
\tag{3}
\]

For this normalization the elementary periodic Ladyzhenskaya estimate

\[
\|u\|_4^2\le10\|u\|_2\|\nabla u\|_2
\tag{4}
\]

is sufficient. For completeness: apply the one-dimensional fundamental theorem to `F=|u|²` in each coordinate to get
`F(x,y)≤(2π)^{-1}∫F(s,y)ds+∫|∂xF(s,y)|ds` and its `y` version. Multiply these bounds, integrate, use Cauchy–Schwarz and `Dx+Dy≤√2||∇u||2`. In normalized norms this gives
`||u||4²≤||u||2²+2√2π||u||2||∇u||2`. Mean-zero Poincaré and `1+2√2π<10` give (4). This proof works for vector fields through `|∂i|u||≤|∂iu|`.

Testing the equation against `A^{-1}u`, integrating the nonlinear term by parts, and using (4) gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\tfrac12Y'+\nu X
&\le \|u\|_4^2\|\nabla A^{-1}u\|_2
\le10\sqrt X\sqrt Z\sqrt Y\\
&\le {\nu\over2}X+{50\over\nu}ZY.
\end{aligned}
\]

Hence

\[
Y'+\nu X\le {100\over\nu}ZY.
\]

An integrating factor and (3) prove the explicit all-time estimate

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
\int_0^\infty\|u(t)\|_2^2\,dt
\le {Y(0)\over\nu}\exp\!\left({50E^2\over\nu^2}\right)
\le {E^2\over\nu(K+1)^2}\exp\!\left({50E^2\over\nu^2}\right).}
\tag{5}
\]

The last inequality uses the **square** cutoff: every nonzero initial coefficient has Euclidean frequency at least `K+1`. No uniform enstrophy or higher regularity bound was added. The proof uses smoothness only to justify the identities; the estimates do not depend on the initial Sobolev norms.

For `B(u,u)=P div(u⊗u)`, convolution and Cauchy–Schwarz imply

\[
|B_j(u,u)|\le |j|X(t).
\tag{6}
\]

Since `u_j(0)=0` for every resolved `j`, its mild formula gives

\[
|u_j(t)|\le |j|\int_0^t X(s)\,ds.
\tag{7}
\]

For an arbitrary fixed square output `P_J`, `J≤K`, define

\[
S_J=\left(\sum_{|j|_\infty\le J}|j|^2\right)^{1/2}
=(2J+1)\sqrt{2J(J+1)/3}.
\]

Equations (3), (5), (7) yield

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|P_Ju(t)\|_2
\le\min\left\{E,\ S_JE^2T,\ {S_JE^2e^{50(E/\nu)^2}\over\nu(K+1)^2}\right\}.}
\tag{8}
\]

For `J=K`, use `S_K≤4K²` and `S_K/(K+1)²≤2` to get

\[
\mathfrak E_K^0\le
\min\{E,4K^2E^2T,2E^2e^{50(E/\nu)^2}/\nu\}.
\tag{9}
\]
